claims.statement: The WMSC historical table names O’Brien as the 1991 champion; the extracted row reports seven competitors.
O’Brien reports leaving school at 16 and beginning memory training at 30 after a 1987 television demonstration.
The governing organisation places the first championship in London in 1991; its current rankings use a 2021 baseline.
Spinks’s round page dates her Bob Graham to 17–18 June 2005 and gives 23:33.
Her later account gives June 2005 and 23:32, one minute different from her round page.
Spinks recalls road running in 2001, then a Trunce advertisement while preparing for the Great North Run by October 2002.
The 2004 organiser’s table lists Nicky Spinks of Penistone eighth, 09:01:12, among 11 finishers and eight retired entries in Heart of Granite.
The 2024 account describes a first-female prize in 2004 while calling Spinks the only woman among 19 entrants. A category prize alone does not establish competitive selectivity.
Spinks reports route reconnaissance and a similar practice circuit from her farm; the dated interview does not quantify her early weekly hours.
The author bibliography lists Starlight on 1 November 1983 and Heartsong on 28 February 1984.
Macomber calls Heartsong her first published book in 1982; that publication claim conflicts with her bibliography.
Macomber recalls selling articles, including one to Woman’s Day for $350, before the novel sale. No article title or acceptance date is supplied.
Macomber recalls rented equipment, household interruptions, studying four novels’ structures, and an editor’s rejection before another publisher bought the manuscript.
Publishers Weekly reports birth in 1948 and Starlight as the first novel in 1983. The year pair implies 34–35 at release, not an exact age or first-acceptance age.
LUP identifies Cleeves’s first published work as a chapter in its 1982 Hilbre volume, preceding her novel debut.
Cleeves recalls being asked by editor J. D. Craggs, a friend through bird-observatory connections, to contribute a human perspective. Commission and acceptance dates are absent.
Cleeves dates Hilbre residence to 1977–1981 and social-work study to the move; she describes diary writing and starting fiction during pregnancy leave.
Roberts and Andrews analyse A year on Hilbre and cite Cleeves’s 1982 chapter at pages 48–64; this independently corroborates attribution and publication, not acceptance timing.
ABC reports Goodwin as the 38-year-old winner on 19 July 2009, with judges George Calombaris, Gary Mehigan and Matt Preston. This dates reporting/broadcast, not filming.
The 2024 interview account reports elected Year 12 school captaincy at Hornsby Girls High School, an earlier selection needing its own threshold audit.
The same account describes interrupted education study, youth-group service, family IT work and creative cooking; it supplies no complete pre-26 achievement inventory.
Goodwin recalls a friend encouraging her application and time away from family and business during the show. Exact practice hours and pre-show paid cooking remain unknown.
